steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, treated vs control, confounded
caveats: The processing batch is perfectly confounded with the condition. Every log2 fold change here is a treated-plus-B2 versus control-plus-B1 difference and cannot be attributed to treatment. This is not fixable by analysis
With 12,000 genes and 6 per group the gene list may be large and largely batch-driven; a large count of significant genes is not evidence of a strong treatment effect
If a fold-change threshold is wanted, pass it as lfcThreshold inside results() rather than filtering the table afterwards
steps.context: Fit DESeq2 on the raw counts from counts.csv with design ~ condition. The batch is perfectly confounded with the condition, so no batch term may be fitted (the model matrix would be rank-deficient) and no count-adjustment method may be used (it would remove the condition effect along with the batch). State the assumption this rests on — that the B1/B2 processing difference contributes nothing — and label every result confounded. Set control explicitly as the reference level of the condition factor rather than relying on alphabetical ordering, and name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated, control) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; do not pre-scale, pre-normalize, or transform the counts before fitting. Keep the Cook's-distance outlier behaviour on — with 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags outlier genes and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts, so report that NA count separately from the NAs produced by independent filtering. The profile names salmon as the count source, but only a gene-level integer matrix was staged: there are no transcript-level quantifications and no per-gene average transcript lengths, so the tximport length-offset route cannot be taken. Record that limitation in the output rather than fabricating offsets.

The rule's named second collection is Reactome, but no Reactome gene-set file is present in this environment — use human GO Biological Process as the second collection and state that substitution; human WikiPathways is available as a further alternative. plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq, batch-confounded
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a raw salmon gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row sample table (metadata.csv) carrying condition and batch. The design is 6 treated vs 6 control, and the processing batch is perfectly confounded with the condition: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 holds all 6 treated samples. That is the fact that shapes the whole plan. No model can separate a treatment effect from a B2-vs-B1 processing effect here, and no repair method can either: a ~ batch + condition design matrix is rank-deficient, and ComBat-seq / removeBatchEffect / SVA would remove the condition effect together with the batch. So the plan fits ~ condition alone, states the untestable assumption it rests on (no batch effect), and labels every result as confounded rather than pretending the estimate is a treatment effect.

T1S1 does sample-structure QC on a blind VST: PCA on the 500 most variable genes and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, coloured by both condition and batch, plus library sizes. Because condition and batch are the same partition of the 12 samples, this step cannot separate them either; its job is to show how much total variance the single B1/B2 = control/treated split explains and whether any sample departs from its group, and to say plainly that the two labellings of the PCA are identical.

T1S2 runs the actual contrast: minimal pre-filter (>= 10 counts in at least 6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model, DESeq2 Wald test on ~ condition with control set explicitly as the reference level and the contrast named condition, treated (numerator) vs control (denominator), apeglm shrinkage for the reported and ranked fold changes, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and the p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment. Since the profile says the counts came from salmon but only a gene-level count matrix was staged (no transcript quantifications, no per-gene average transcript lengths), the length-offset import route is unavailable; the step must state that and proceed on the supplied integer matrix.

T1S3 is the robustness check the two-method rule asks for: an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same counts and the same one-factor design, reporting each method's count and the intersection as the high-confidence set. With 6 per group the two tools should agree on most genes; disagreement concentrates at low counts. This does nothing about the confounding — both methods estimate the same confounded quantity — and the step says so.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes into fgsea. The ranking statistic is a disputed choice and this plan states it: the DESeq2 Wald statistic, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, which the unshrunken log2 fold change is not and a saturating signed p-value is not. Hallmark first (human, 50 sets), then the human GO Biological Process collection as the second, more specific pass — the seed's reference census carries no Reactome GMT, and GO BP is the staged human follow-up collection the enrichment rule names alongside Reactome and WikiPathways; WikiPathways human is also staged as a fallback. Pathway-level results inherit the confounding exactly as the gene-level ones do.

T1S4 assembles the report and is where the confounding is stated as the headline finding rather than a footnote: what was run, package versions, the design, thresholds, genes tested, genes called, MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram, both shrunken and unshrunken fold changes with standard errors, the edgeR overlap, the leading-edge genes of each significant set, and an explicit statement that every differential call is a treatment-plus-batch effect that this experiment cannot decompose, with the design change (batches spanning both conditions, or technical replicates across batches) that would fix it.

Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples
Median-of-ratios size factors inside the model

Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which hallmark and GO biological-process gene sets are coordinately shifted between treated (B2) and control (B1) lung samples, on the full ranked list of tested genes?
steps.context: Take the complete DESeq2 results table from T1S2 — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank it by the Wald statistic (the stat column). The ranking metric is a disputed choice and this plan states its side: the Wald statistic, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, unlike the unshrunken fold change (large and noisy at low counts) and unlike a signed p-value (which saturates and produces arbitrary ties at the top). Run fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark collection first, with gene sets restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes, BH adjustment, and a fixed random seed recorded for the permutations. Then run a second, more specific pass against the human GO Biological Process collection. Both reference collections are human gene-symbol GMTs and the count matrix already uses gene symbols, so the identifier spaces match directly; if a mapping step is nonetheless used, report the share of tested genes that failed to map. The rule's named second collection is Reactome, but no Reactome gene-set file is present in this environment — use human GO Biological Process as the second collection and state that substitution; human WikiPathways is available as a further alternative. If neither follow-up collection can be resolved at run time, report the hallmark pass alone and record the absence rather than failing the step. Collapse significant sets that share most of their leading-edge genes into groups and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list: the ranked method on the full list is the planned approach, and an ORA of a short list has no power.

Includes the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, and the permutation seed.

steps.name: Confounded-design report
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control lung expression from this experiment, and what design would be needed to answer the question properly?
steps.context: Assemble the QC (T1S1), the DESeq2 results (T1S2), the edgeR cross-check (T1S3), and the enrichment (T2S1) into one report. The headline is the design, not the gene list: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated samples, so the treatment effect and the processing effect are the same contrast and no analysis can separate them. State the assumption the results rest on — that the B1/B2 processing difference contributes nothing to expression — say that it is untestable with these samples, and label every gene and every pathway accordingly. Then give the reproducibility and methods record: package versions and sessionInfo, the random seed used for the GSEA permutations, the gene-set collection name and version, the design formula, the named contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested, and the number called per method. Include the MA plot, the dispersion plot and the p-value histogram before the gene tables. In the gene table give the unshrunken log2 fold change, the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, and the lfcSE for each gene, and rank the table and the plots by the shrunken value. Give the DESeq2/edgeR overlap counts and the leading-edge genes of each reported gene set. Close with the concrete design fix: batches that each span both conditions, or a set of technical replicates processed across both batches, either of which would make the batch effect estimable.
steps.description: A standalone report whose primary conclusion is that the treated-vs-control comparison is confounded with processing batch and therefore not interpretable as a treatment effect, accompanied by the full confounded results (gene tables with shrunken and unshrunken fold changes, fit diagnostics, method overlap, enriched sets with leading edges) and a reproducibility record.
